newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysia Railway hands out S'pore eviction notices.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Railway hands out S'pore eviction notices.

text.p: The Malaysian railway company KTM Berhad said on Saturday it had issued 168 eviction notices against people occupying its land in Singapore.
The announcement followed news reports in Malaysia, denied by the government, that Kuala Lumpur had decided to freeze all new bilateral dealings with Singapore.

The row stemmed from an affidavit by Singapore elder statesman Lee Kuan Yew calling a southern Malaysian state notorious for crime. Lee twice apologised for the accusation, but the issue has refused to go away.
"We have since determined precisely the extent of illegal occupation on our property," the general manager of KTM's Property Management department, said in a statement.

The operation to issue the notices, which began on Thursday and ended on Saturday, was launched against private operators who used KTM's land as dumping grounds, storage yards, make-shift housing for foreign workers and as scrap metal yards.
The squatters were given seven days to leave the properties or face charges for damages, trespass and legal costs, the KTM statement said.
KTM owns more than 200 hectares (500 acres) of land in Singapore on a 999-year lease dating back to the time when both were still British colonies.
